title: Room and Visitor
premise: Urban explorer Casper Coldharbour discovers unmapped tunnels beneath the derelict Coldharbour estate he inherited, and begins recording himself sleeping to document his sleepwalking. The recordings reveal a second voice — patient, courteous, asking questions only the dead founders of his family would know. As Casper deciphers the founders' unfinished ritual, he realizes the 'visitor' is a hungering presence they bound with their own memories, and that his inheritance was never property but a duty: to feed it a lifetime of recollection or let it loose. In the end, Casper completes the ritual by surrendering every memory of his mother, sealing the visitor but leaving himself a stranger to his own past.
about_author: O. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing basements, vaults, and sealed floors of condemned municipal buildings. Their fiction draws on the conviction that old structures remember more than the people who pay to forget them.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mapping the Coldharbour estate's documented cellars, Casper finds a doorway whose measurements contradict every survey — a tunnel that shouldn't exist, breathing warm air. He counts doors as a habit of control; tonight the count comes back wrong. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into the first cold drop of dread.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishing his rituals: every light burning, doors tallied hourly, chalk marks on thresholds. His lawyer calls about probate papers mentioning an 'obligation' attached to the estate that no one will explain. Emotional beat: compulsive order as armor against a house that seems to rearrange itself when unobserved.

chapters.title: The Sleep Recordings
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. After waking with chalk dust on his hands and mud on his feet, he sets a recorder running overnight. Playback captures him sleepwalking — and then a second voice, dry and courteous, asking him questions: names, dates, who buried what beneath the east stair. Emotional beat: horror at hearing himself answer in a voice not entirely his own.

chapters.title: Questions Answered in Sleep
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Casper's waking self transcribing tapes and fragmented dream-sequences where the Visitor interviews him gently, like a doctor taking history. Each answer loosens something in his waking memory — he can no longer recall his mother's face. Emotional beat: grief disguised as curiosity, the first real cost.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with ledger excerpts in the founders' voices. In the estate archive he finds the ritual text: four founders bound a presence beneath the house using pooled memories as mortar, renewing it each generation. The last entry is his grandfather's, dated the year he vanished. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as sentence, not gift.

chapters.title: What the Tunnels Want
chapters.summary: Casper descends into the unmapped tunnels with the ledger, following warm air. The walls are inscribed with questions in his own handwriting, decades older than him. The Visitor speaks openly now, offering bargains: give me your worst memory and keep the pleasant ones. Emotional beat: temptation — power offered as relief.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol Vega, an elderly former tenant who lived on the estate as a girl. She tells Casper about the night his grandfather 'went down to settle accounts,' and warns that the Visitor doesn't want memories — it wants the self they're carved from. Emotional beat: an ally's terror, and the revelation that Casper is already half-spent.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The recordings now show conversations lasting full nights; he wakes thinner, grayer, missing whole years of recollection. The house's lights fail one wing at a time, and the door count climbs past what the floor plan allows. Emotional beat: panic and resolve fused — he must finish the ritual before nothing remains to finish it with.

chapters.title: The Ritual of the Founders
chapters.summary: Climax. Casper's POV, descending to the binding chamber with Marisol holding the ledger open above. The ritual requires one heir to pour their dearest memories into the seal willingly. The Visitor offers a final bargain — his mother's face for his survival. Casper refuses the trade and gives everything of her instead. Emotional beat: sacrificial love weaponized against hunger.

chapters.title: A Stranger to His Own Past
chapters.summary: Resolution, Casper's POV. The tunnels are cold now, the doors count true, the lights stay off without fear. Casper keeps the estate, keeps the rituals, keeps a photograph of a woman he knows he loved but cannot see. Marisol visits; he asks her to tell him about his mother, and listens like a stranger. Emotional beat: quiet, earned sorrow — victory that costs the victor his heart's own history.
